title: Fenn and the Flying Tart
markdown:
In a cozy little cottage, the kind where the teacups hum happy tunes and the bread always smells like sunshine, lived a very sweet fawn named Fenn. Fenn had ears that wiggled like little dancers when he was happy, and a heart as soft as a dandelion puff. He loved to explore the cottage, peeking into teacups and sniffing flowerpots. But sometimes Fenn’s wobbly legs would get tangled in the soft rug. Boink. He’d do a little flip. He’d land softly. His nose would twitch. Then he’d hop up, ready to try again. He had big curious eyes that missed nothing, not a single crumb or a glimmer of sunshine.

And in that same cottage, flying around like a happy little hum, lived Marzipan. Marzipan was not just any pixie. She was a kitchen pixie. Her wings sparkled like spilled sugar. They showed all the colors of the rainbow when the light hit them. And her nose? Oh, her nose was a marvel. It could sniff out a cookie crumb from far away, or even a tiny drop of jam hiding under the table. She wore a tiny cherry-red apron that was always dusted with flour. She zipped around the kitchen, making sure everything was just right, always with a cheerful, “Chirp chirp. Ready for magic.”

One sunny morning, the kind of morning where sunbeams tickled your nose, Marzipan was baking. Oh, what was she baking? A plum tart, of course. This tart was going to be extra special. It had a secret ingredient. It was cinnamon stardust. Marzipan found it in a tiny sparkly jar in the pantry. “Just a tiny pinch,” she giggled to herself, her nose twitching with delight as she sprinkled it in. Poof. The cinnamon stardust shimmered and wiggled with its own special magic. It smelled like a warm hug, a summer breeze, and a dash of happy giggles all mixed together.

Suddenly, the tart on the cooling rack gave a little shudder. Then it wobbled like jelly on a plate. And then it started to roll. It was not just rolling, oh no. It was rolling with purpose, zooming this way and that across the smooth wooden counter. It seemed to be following a super-duper yummy smell: the cinnamon stardust. It smelled so good, so exciting, the tart itself could not help but follow its own delicious trail.

Marzipan nearly bumped her head on a sugar bowl. Fenn, who was happily munching on a dandelion nearby, looked up with his big curious eyes. His ears gave a little twitch. “What is happening, Marzipan?” he asked, his voice a gentle bleat. He had never seen a tart move on its own before.

“The tart. It is enchanted,” Marzipan giggled, a sound like tiny bells tinkling. “It is chasing the cinnamon stardust smell. We have to follow it, Fenn. Come on.”

And so the grand chase began. The plum tart, with its golden crust and plump plums, zoomed under the kitchen table. Whizz. Fenn’s legs were a bit long. He had to step very carefully over it. He bent his knees like a dancer, trying not to squish a ladybug. Step, step, wobble. He managed it perfectly. Marzipan, with her tiny shimmering wings, flew right over. “You can do it, Fenn,” she cheered, doing a little loop-de-loop just to show off.

The tart then zoomed past a broom. The broom looked very important, standing guard in the corner. Swoosh. “Whoa there, little tart. Careful now,” Marzipan called out, doing a quick little zig-zag to avoid the broom bristles. Fenn had to do a funny little sidestep, like a crab walking sideways on the beach. Scuttle, scuttle. He nearly giggled out loud, his legs doing a funny little jig. “This is like a grand adventure,” Fenn said, his ears perked up like little antennas. But where is it going? He looked around, his big eyes trying to follow the speedy tart.

“I think it is going towards the sunny spot by the window,” Marzipan chirped, her voice full of excitement. “That is where the cinnamon stardust smell is strongest. It must love the sunshine.”

The tart rolled and rolled, a blur of golden crust and juicy plums, past the rumbling oven and under the cheerful chimes of the clock. It was heading towards the big comfy armchair, the one with the soft squishy cushions where they often had story time. The armchair was a bit lumpy. Sometimes little things, like buttons or crumbs, got lost behind it. “Oh dear,” whispered Fenn, his ears drooping just a tiny bit. He did not want the tart to get lost.

“We have to catch it before it gets lost behind there,” Marzipan said, her sparkly wings fluttering with concern. “It might get shy and hide. Fenn, can you try and nudge it gently towards me? I will try and scoop it up with my apron. I have got my best apron on for this.” Fenn took a deep breath. His nose twitched. He had a job to do. Helping his friend made his wobbly legs feel steadier. He carefully walked towards the rolling tart, his steps becoming more sure. He gave the tart a gentle nudge with his soft velvety nose. Boop. The tart wobbled a bit more, almost as if it was playing a game of tag with Fenn’s nose.

Marzipan swooped in with her apron held out like a tiny magical net, her sparkly wings creating a gentle breeze. She managed to catch the rolling tart just as it was about to slip behind the armchair. It landed softly in her apron. She was so happy and relieved. Her wings fluttered with triumph. Fenn trotted over, his tail giving a happy wag that made his whole body wiggle. “We did it,” he said, his voice full of pride. “We caught the runaway tart.”

Marzipan carefully placed the tart back on the table, right in the middle of the sunny spot by the window. It seemed to be settled now, its magical rolling all done, as if it had simply wanted to explore the cottage a little bit. The scent of cinnamon stardust still filled the air, smelling even more delicious now after the exciting chase.

“That was so much fun,” Fenn said, giving Marzipan a gentle thankful nuzzle. He loved adventures, especially with his best pixie friend.

“It was,” Marzipan agreed, her sparkly wings giving a happy little shimmy. “And you know what makes adventures even better?” Fenn looked at her, his big curious eyes shining with anticipation. “What?”

“Sharing the yummy rewards,” Marzipan declared, her voice bubbling with joy. She scurried over to the tart and, with a tiny enchanted knife, cut them both a big warm slice. The crust was perfectly crispy, the plums were sweet and juicy, and the cinnamon stardust made it taste like pure warm magic. Fenn took a big bite, and his eyes squeezed shut with delight. Marzipan nibbled hers happily, a smear of plum juice appearing on her cherry-red apron.

They sat together, side-by-side, munching on the most delicious plum tart in the whole wide world. A crumb of cinnamon stardust caught the window light and stayed there, still, as if the tart had finished its walk and was glad to be a tart again.
